acme_data_team: hey team — after our scheduled pin update this morning our downstream indexers started failing. our stored embeddings are 512d but the /embeddings call is returning 768-length vectors. rolling back is urgent, any ideas?

sarah_support: sorry to hear that. can you paste the API response you got and the model param you pinned to?

acme_data_team: here's the request we send (node):
```js
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer xxxxx' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'rf-embed-512:stable', input: ['doc1'] })
});
```
and the response snippet:
```json
{ "data": [{ "embedding": [0.0012, 0.0023, ..., 0.1234], "length": 768 }], "model": "open-embed-wide-768@2026-03-12" }
```

acme_data_team: we pinned alias `rf-embed-512:stable` in our account months ago. looked unchanged in UI.

raj_engineer: thanks — quick look at catalog shows `rf-embed-512:stable` was recently repointed to a variant alias that can fall back to a higher-capacity build during canary/scale operations. that fallback path returns 768 dims.

raj_engineer: root cause is alias fallthrough during capacity routing + a model variant mismatch in the alias mapping. the pinned name was an alias, not an immutable model SHA.

acme_data_team: oh — we assumed alias == immutable. how do we force exactly 512 now while you fix mapping?

sarah_support: immediate mitigations: 1) use an exact model version (the immutable id) instead of the alias, e.g. `rf-embed-512@sha-0a1b2c3d`. 2) If you can't change callers quickly, set a tenant-level enforcement flag to reject embeddings not equal to 512 (we can enable on your org) so requests fail instead of returning 768s.

acme_data_team: can you enable the enforcement flag? we need to fail-safe while you revert the alias.

raj_engineer: yes — I can flip org-enforce-embedding-dim=512 for cust-acme. dave, can infra confirm we can toggle without a deploy?

Dave_infra: deploy-bot: toggling feature flag for org cust-acme now.

deploy-bot: feature-flag change recorded: org=cust-acme, flag=org-enforce-embedding-dim, value=512, changed_by=raj_engineer, ts=2460124000

acme_data_team: got it — after flag flip we started seeing explicit 400 responses instead of silent 768 vectors. that's safe for us. thanks.

raj_engineer: long-term fix: we'll 1) update alias mapping to point `rf-embed-512:stable` to the immutable 512 build (sha) and 2) add a catalog invariant check that rejects alias repoints that change public vector dimensionality without an explicit major-version bump. I'm opening an internal PR for that.

raj_engineer: repro steps we used to validate:
```bash
# request that triggers fallthrough path (simulated low-capacity canary)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rf-embed-512:stable","input":["x"]}' | jq .model
# returned: "open-embed-wide-768@2026-03-12"
```

sarah_support: notes for the support playbook: - ask for exact model string and the `model` field in the response - look for mismatch between alias and returned model - offer immediate org-enforce flag or exact-sha pin - escalate catalog repoint to eng if dims differ

acme_data_team: appreciated. timeline for alias revert?

raj_engineer: will push catalog revert and invariant check in next 2 business days. once done we'll notify and you can unpin or revert to alias safely.

acme_data_team: great — thanks for the fast turnaround. last ask: can we get a short note we can send to our devs explaining why pins vs aliases matter?

sarah_support: sending brief explainer now:
```
Short note: Aliases (e.g., rf-embed-512:stable) are editable pointers to underlying model builds and can be repointed for rollouts. Immutable model IDs (sha IDs or timestamped builds) never change. For production systems that rely on exact embedding dimensionality, pin to the immutable model ID. If you must use aliases, enable org-level dim enforcement to avoid silent shape changes.
```

acme_data_team: perfect. closing once you confirm revert.

raj_engineer: will follow up in this thread when catalog revert is complete.
